clue.text: Accept without questioning name of bird

definitions.meaning: to take something in without doubt or protest, as one gulps down a claim
a fork-tailed migrant that skims over fields in summer

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take a bird's name on trust.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to believe something credulously, the other names a familiar migratory songbird with a forked tail.

clue.text: Odds on Australian man not starting to smarten up

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the betting odds at the off

indicators.note: not starting says the first letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Bruce is the stock name for an Australian man

explanation.surface: Betting on an Australian man who fails to start, to smarten him up.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is the bookmaker's starting price; Bruce is the stock jokey name for an Australian bloke.
explanation.definitionFit: To neaten oneself or a place, as in tidying up for a visitor.

clue.text: Capital poultry at first

indicators.note: first says the short word at comes before the birds

parts.note: hens are farmyard poultry

explanation.surface: Poultry coming first in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece's capital city.

clue.text: Generous political philosophy

parts.note: liberal can mean generous or open-handed, so the clue reads as an open-handed outlook, while also naming the doctrine of individual freedom

explanation.surface: Describing an open-handed system of political thought.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine favouring individual freedom, tolerance and reform, built on a word that also means open-handed.

clue.text: Initially wonder cure could be mine

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word wonder

parts.note: to cure is to heal

explanation.surface: A miracle cure might be mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like the possessive but is a noun: this word for a Cornish mine is in the Telegraph's crossword stock. Cornwall is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cornish dialect word for a tin or copper pit.

clue.text: Strike feline

definitions.meaning: an unofficial walkout by workers, called without union backing
an untamed small cat of European woodland

explanation.surface: A walkout led by a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: An unofficial industrial stoppage shares its name with the untamed small cat of Europe and Scotland.

clue.text: American perhaps you and I back expressing reluctance

parts.note: we means you and I together
the stern is the back of a ship
er is the hesitant noise of someone unwilling

explanation.surface: An American, perhaps, while the two of us hang back reluctantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the western world, or the western states, of which an American is an example.

clue.text: Green cloth?

definitions.meaning: a grassy expanse, as in a bowling green
a fine linen or cotton fabric

explanation.surface: Asking about a green cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of mown grass, and a fine sheer linen fabric, share the name.

clue.text: Doctrine fabricated in Devon

indicators.note: fabricated means made up, so the letters of doctrine are built into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctrine invented somewhere in the south-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; the definition says only that the answer is found there.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town north-west of Exeter, in that county.

clue.text: Note river in meandering estuary

indicators.note: in places the river's letter inside the jumbled word
meandering means wandering, so the letters of estuary twist into a new order

explanation.surface: A note about a river winding through an estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meandering' turns ESTUARY into TEASURY, and 'in' puts R after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A Treasury note was a British banknote issued by the government finance department in the First World War.

clue.text: Bertha loses shirt going round treatment centre

indicators.note: spinning round suggests the remaining letters of the name are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: a T-shirt gives T, the letter Bertha is said to lose

explanation.surface: Bertha has lost her shirt somewhere on the way round a clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T (for T-shirt) from BERTHA to leave BERHA, and 'going round' rearranges those five letters; 'loses' tells you the T comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for rehabilitation, it is a clinic where people recover from addiction.

clue.text: Lee's moved to unknown place that's neither here nor there

indicators.note: moved says the letters of Lee's are shifted round into a new order

parts.note: the question word asking for a location not yet known

explanation.surface: A man called Lee has moved house to some unknown place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges LEES (the 's is a letter here) into ELSE, then the question word for an unknown location follows. The definition plays on the idiom meaning 'irrelevant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere other than this spot or that one is, literally, in some other location altogether.

clue.text: Official regulator

definitions.meaning: a person in charge of a department or of finances
a device that governs speed, flow or temperature

explanation.surface: An official who regulates.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a person managing a firm's accounts and a device governing a machine's operation carry this title.

clue.text: Feel the loss of a young lady

definitions.meaning: the title for an unmarried girl or woman

explanation.surface: Someone pines for an absent young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for someone gone, and the courtesy title for an unmarried girl, share one spelling.

clue.text: Outstanding award in city getting medal first for rod-like structure

indicators.note: first says the honour's letters lead the whole word

parts.note: CH, Companion of Honour, a British honour taken loosely as a medal

indicators.note: in puts the outstanding award inside the city

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital city
o/s is the accounting abbreviation for an outstanding balance
OM, the Order of Merit, is a British award

explanation.surface: A fine prize in a city goes to a medal winner first.
explanation.walkthrough: OS and OM go between ROM and E of ROME, behind CH. CH (Companion of Honour) and OM (Order of Merit) are British honours.
explanation.definitionFit: A thread-shaped body in the cell nucleus carrying genes.

clue.text: Nearly too late just before lunchtime perhaps

definitions.meaning: literally the clock period ending at noon, when many people eat

explanation.surface: Something happens at the last minute, right before lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for the last possible moment, read literally, is the sixty minutes leading up to midday.

clue.text: Provide as remedy having sprayed

indicators.note: to remedy is to put right, so the letters of provide as are set into a corrected order

explanation.surface: Providing something as a cure after spraying it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remedy' rearranges the nine letters of PROVIDE AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Turned into a fine mist or gas, as an atomiser does to liquid.

clue.text: Scaly cat losing its tail to animal in Australia

parts.note: platy describes rock made of flat plates or flakes

indicators.note: losing its tail says the final letter of the cat word is dropped

parts.note: puss is a familiar name for a cat

explanation.surface: A scaly cat without its tail turns into an Australian creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck-billed egg-laying mammal of eastern Australia.

clue.text: Runners jump on inclined surface

parts.note: skis are runners that slide over snow
lope is a long bounding stride

explanation.surface: Runners leap on a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' suggests athletes; here it means the blades on which one glides over snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowy hillside piste for gliding down, which is necessarily on a slant.

clue.text: Larger stretch of water?

parts.note: superior can mean greater, so the clue reads as a body of water bigger than another, while really naming the largest of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Asking for a bigger body of water.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: the North American lake's name, read as ordinary English, means a higher or greater lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The biggest of North America's Great Lakes has a name that literally means a higher or greater body of water.

clue.text: Gloomy part of island is malodorous

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a smelly island is dreary.
explanation.definitionFit: Depressing and dreary, like a wet bleak day.

clue.text: System of acting

parts.note: the technique of performing devised by Stanislavski, whose name is also an everyday word for any orderly procedure

explanation.surface: A technique for performing on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanislavski-derived approach in which performers draw on their own emotions; in general an orderly procedure.

clue.text: Old news agency thanks secret service

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
SS, the abbreviation for a secret service

explanation.surface: A defunct press agency thanks the spies.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for 'thanks'.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the official Soviet press bureau, since renamed, hence 'old'.

clue.text: River in public transport route can be jumped over!

indicators.note: in says the river sits inside the transport route

parts.note: a tramline is the track a tram runs along
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A river lies across a tram route, and you can leap over it.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark marks a cheeky definition: you bounce up and over on a sprung mat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprung canvas sheet on a frame is something gymnasts bounce on and leap above.

clue.text: Additional southern customs

parts.note: more means extra or additional

explanation.surface: Extra rules of the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin-derived term for the established conventions and traditions of a society.

clue.text: Mariner went after his Excellency to the island

indicators.note: went after says the sailor comes behind the ambassador

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for His Excellency, an ambassador's title
RM, a Royal Marine

explanation.surface: A sailor followed the ambassador out to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: RM is a Royal Marine; the answer is a small Channel Island near Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: A small car-free Channel Island lying off Guernsey.

clue.text: Posers for replacement teacher

indicators.note: replacement says the letters of posers and for are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: Puzzling questions set for a supply teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' rearranges the nine letters of POSERS FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A university academic of the highest rank, who lectures and teaches students.

clue.text: Repeatedly having no speed or vitality

indicators.note: repeatedly says the letter for no is written twice over

parts.note: O stands for nought, nothing
mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

explanation.surface: Someone always lacking speed or liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for energy, zest and attractive force.

clue.text: Cooked me instead!

indicators.note: the word instead is split so its first two letters act as a container signal

parts.note: stead means place, as in 'in his stead'

explanation.surface: Someone protests that they were cooked rather than the dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'instead' as 'in stead': ME goes in STEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Food cooked over boiling water has been prepared by vapour.

clue.text: Bombarded once natural cover had been removed

definitions.text: once natural cover had been removed
definitions.meaning: with the husk or pod stripped off, as with peas or nuts

explanation.surface: Something was bombarded after its natural cover had gone.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is attacked with artillery rounds, the other is having had its husk or pod stripped away, like peas.
